_about: Per-video settings for scripts/youtube-publish.py. Edit titles, tags and dates here; the description is built from video/DESCRIPTION.md, the blurb below and the track's credit in video/music/CREDITS.md. privacy: private | unlisted | public; publishAt (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-27T15:00:00-03:00) schedules a private video to go public then. fullVideo: once the long video is up, put its link here and run --update: every description gets 'Watch the full video: <link>'. YouTube counts a vertical video as a Short only up to 3:00.

videos.title: The Triangle of Everything
videos.blurb: There's a single image that contains everything. All objects, all the sciences, all the history from the big bang to the death of the universe. I've been obsessed with this one chart for years now and spent countless hours designing many different ways to see it – now it's your time to get hooked.

videos.title: The Atomic Diagonal
videos.blurb: From a milliliter of water up the density line: what sinks and floats, animals, buildings, and the rocks and small moons where gravity starts to take over.

videos.title: The Super-Jupiter Vertical
videos.blurb: Where gravity takes over: round worlds, atmospheres, Earth's Goldilocks zone, gas giants, and the brown dwarfs where the line splits.

videos.title: The Atomic Diagonal
videos.blurb: If you plot everything in a log scale of mass and size, most things will fall on this diagonal line. What does it mean? This line contains many stories: about the things that fall to each of its sides, and for things that don't follow it at all.

videos.title: The Life and Death of Stars
videos.blurb: The Triangle of Everything is a log chart of mass and size, but it's also a story about the life and death of stars, how they are born, how they evolve and how sometimes they die in the most spectacular and mysterious objects of them all.

videos.title: The Black Hole Line
videos.blurb: The top-left limit of everything and why it is 45°, TON 618, the window for primordial black holes, galaxies without their dark matter, and the lucky few survivors.

videos.title: The Black Hole Slope
videos.blurb: Every black hole sits on the same line of the Triangle of Everything, from the ones dying stars leave behind to TON 618, whose event horizon is bigger than Pluto's orbit. And the bigger they get, the less dense they are.

videos.title: Why nothing can be bigger than the Hubble sphere
videos.blurb: Bigger means emptier, the second edge of the triangle, the edge of our own universe, why it sits on the black-hole line, and the observable universe as a history of our own past.
